correctness.rationale: For independent exchangeable (r_i,p_i) pairs with no within-pair ties and distinct minima m_i=min(r_i,p_i), conditional on unordered pairs the orientations are independent fair binary coins. Diamond D=max m_i, while Box B is 1 when no r_i>p_i, else the smallest m_i among those orientations. Thus of the 2^n equiprobable orientations exactly one yields B>D, one yields B=D (only maximizing index reversed), and all remaining yield B<D, proving distribution-free (2^-n,2^-n,1-2^(1-n)) and independence of category from unordered pair data including D, also n=1. Under 2n iid atomless common-F inputs, uniform probability-integral transform gives Pr(F(B)>u,F(D)<=v)=[h(v)+max(0,h(v)-h(u))]^n, h(t)=t-t²/2. The two singular cumulative components F(B)=1 and F(B)=F(D) each have mass h(v)^n; differentiating the open-wedge survival-CDF gives density 2n(n-1)(1-u)(1-v)(2h(v)-h(u))^{n-2}. With u=s/n, v=1-t/√n, the joint survival limit is exp(-s-t²), yielding independent exponential and Rayleigh-type extremes. Independent exact orientation enumeration checked all 2^n orientations for 1<=n<=11; finite computations corroborate, not replace, the probability and asymptotic proof.

Random fuzzy matrix work analyzes max-min closure rather than jointly sampled modal evaluations. The distribution-free symmetry trichotomy, two singular masses, full rank-coordinate joint density and independent extreme scales were not seen in inspected same-semantics and nearby probability papers. Search cannot prove absolute priority; general order-statistics literature may contain a translated equivalent.

value.rationale: The basic Box/Diamond order comparison under random exchangeable fuzzy evidence is a natural probabilistic semantics invariant. Exact positive-probability equality in atomless inputs, its exponential rarity with n, the two singular components, and distinct independent n versus sqrt(n) fluctuation scales provide substantive information beyond a routine independence check. The restrictions on conditional symmetry/no ties distinguish the theorem from general fuzzy-frame validity.
